exercises.title: Improvement 1 — which process do requirements feed?
exercises.problemHtml:
Figure 31-1: requirements are at the heart of a project and feed planning, tracking and control, change control, acceptance and system testing, construction, and user documentation. Which process does each effect describe?

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Yêu cầu nuôi các quy trình khác của dự án.

Yêu cầu

  • Trả lời mọi câu trong khung trả lời rồi bấm Nộp.
  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

exercises.title: Improvement 2 — understanding resistance
exercises.problemHtml:
Changing requirements processes changes how stakeholder groups interact, and people dislike being pushed out of their comfort zone. Much resistance comes from fear of the unknown: communicate the rationale and the benefits each group will gain. People ask "What’s in it for me?" — the pay-off (less rework, lower support costs, more customer value) may not be immediate.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Hiểu nguồn gốc kháng cự; trả lời "tôi được gì?".

Yêu cầu

  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

exercises.title: Improvement 3 — real management commitment?
exercises.problemHtml:
Figure 31-3: commitment is what management does, not what it says — funding training and review time, protecting requirements activities from schedule pressure, taking part in prioritisation, holding people accountable for following the process. Which behaviours show real commitment?

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
